warnings: No explicit ASME/ANSI/ISO/DIN standard designation is printed. Inch dimensions, third-angle projection, and legacy US GD&T notation are explicit; drawing_standard is therefore left blank rather than asserted.
Title block identifies TOOL No. SB 14306, MODEL No. 400 SBX, date 7-2-84, drawn B. LATISLAW, checked JWZ, sheet size D, scale HALF. Revision and sheet number/count are not supplied legibly.
Surface-finish numbers 63 and 250 are recorded as printed. Microinch roughness is inferred from US inch-drawing convention; the drawing does not explicitly print the roughness unit or parameter.

Angular dimensions and equal-spacing entries use numeric degrees. The provided dimension-unit enum has no degree option, so the obligatory inch unit field must not be used to interpret angular numbers.

The main body cannot safely be generated as a simple cylinder: it has a controlled taper, stepped internal and external profiles, a rear web, two distinct keyway systems, and 24 flexible finger stations.

The axial depth of the four 1.001 radial end-face keyways is not unambiguously recoverable from this scan. Do not substitute the .437 depth of the distinct 1.005 outer axial keyways. Human resolution is required before a production model.

The peripheral .755 notches and the .500 relief/.125 sawcut detail require confirmation of their longitudinal extents and cut directions from the original drawing. The oblique detail is not a fully dimensioned standalone section.

Hole instance_positions use the lower-left of the nominal 21.500 reference circular envelope: edge coordinates = center coordinates + [10.750,10.750]. These are derived edge coordinates; controlling hole positions are center-referenced. The reference outside diameter must not become a controlling hole-location datum.

The eight .750-10 holes are not an eight-hole 45° equal-spacing pattern. They occupy (±3,±5.196) and (±5.196,±3), giving alternating nominal 30°/60° intervals. 2*sqrt(3^2+5.196^2) = approximately 11.999736, consistent with the 12.00 reference bolt circle.
The eight .375-16 holes form four radial pairs, not one equal-radius bolt circle. Inner radius 5.125 is derived from 7.125 minus 2.000.
Thread series, fit class, tap-drill sizes, and entrance chamfers are not specified. Hole-callout diameters are nominal thread major diameters, not drilling diameters.
The 18.254 bore is before SURFALLOY; the final coated bore is 18.250 +.001/-.000. They are sequential manufacturing states, not separate simultaneous surfaces.

The .500 diameter rolls and 22.405 over-roll diameter describe inspection tooling and measurement; neither should be added as part material. Taper placement must satisfy the over-roll measurement, not merely the 21.500 reference diameter.

Datum B is the rear end face, perpendicular to datum A within .001. The taper has .001 T.I.R. runout to A; the 19.999 cylinder has .001 concentricity to A; the inner rear-web face has .001 parallelism to B.
General note requires all keyways in line, centered and/or square to each other within .001. No datum frame is attached to this note.
Starred radii are high-stress areas: blend smoothly, remove all tool marks, polish if necessary. General break-all-sharp-corners note has no numerical size.

Build order is a CAD dependency order, not a manufacturing routing. Drawing explicitly requires ALL MACHINING TO BE DONE BEFORE SAWCUT; perform finishing operations before sawing in the actual process.

Derived axial closure values are nominal arithmetic only, with no independently assigned tolerances. In particular 3.00, 1.00, and 3.62 do not share consecutive endpoints; their .38 difference is not evidence of a drawing error.
